Mahmudul Islam, Senior Advocate instructed by Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Appellants 
Dr. M. Zahir, Senior Advocate with Mr. Abdur Rahim and Mr. Zafarullah Chowdhury, Advocates instructed by Mrs. Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record ------ For Respondent No.3 
For Respondent Nos. 1-2 ------ None represented.
parties:
G. M. Salehuddin Ahmed and others ------ Appellants
Vs.
Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
3. In the writ petition, it was stated, inter-alia, that the property scheduled for auction in the auction sale notice published in the 'Daily Amardesh' dated 18.08.2006 and in schedule-`Kha' to the plaint of Artha Rin Suit No. 9 of 1991 of the Court of Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Joypurhat (hereinafter referred to as the property in question) was leased out. by the then Dacca Improvement Trust (DIT) now Rajdhani Unnayan ' Kartipakkha (RAJUK) to one Qazi Mesbahuzzaman for 99 years by registered deed of lease being No. 10973 dated `1 30.07.1963. Qazi Mesbahuzzaman sold the property in question to one A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed by registered deed No. 7392 dated 24.09.1971 and his name was mutated with DIT as evidenced by Memo No. DIT/EO/1489 dated 26.11.1971. A.B. M. Shafiquddin Ahmed gifted the property in question to his wife, Hosna Maksuda Hena Ahmed orally and her name was duly mutated with Da vide Memo No. DIT/EO/729 dated 05.07.1972. Later on, Hosna Maksuda Hena Ahmed generally gifted the property in question to her two sons, Abrar Atric Ahmed and Esrar Abin Ahmed and their names were mutated with RAJUK vide Memo No.  RAJUK/ESTATE/141 dated 16.01.1992. Abrar Atric Ahmed and Esrar Abin Ahmed appointed their father, A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed as their duly constituted attorney by registered power of attorney being No. 22 dated 03.01.1994 giving him power to manage and transfer the property in question, which was duly  accepted/approved by RAJUK vide Memo No.  RAJUK/ESTATE/31781 dated 01.08.1994. Abrar Atric Ahmed and Esrar Abin Ahmed, through their attorney, A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed, sold the property in question to Green Garden Housing Limited (hereinafter referred to as Green Housing) by registered deed No. 2923 dated 28.02.1995 upon obtaining k RAJUK's permission by Memo No.  RAJUK/ESTATE/542 dated 16.02.1995. The property in question was mutated in the name of Green Housing vide Mutation Case No. 12952 of 1996. Green Housing constructed a 6-storied building on the property in question with 20 apartments as per the plan approved by RAJUK. Of the above 20 apartments,  Green Housing sold 12 apartments to the petitioners along with proportionate undivided and undemarcated shares in the I property by registered deed being Nos. 7207, 7208, 7204, 7210, 7209, 7206, 7205, 7202, 7201, 7212 and 7211 dated 05.06.2003 and 13041 dated 08.10.2004. The particulars of the flats purchased by each of the petitioners were shown in the cause title of the writ petition against their names. The said transfers took place upon payment of transfer fee to RAJUK and upon obtaining permission from it by Memos dated 05.05.2003 and 01.01.2003. The names of the petitioners have been duly mutated as owners of the flats and co-owners of the property in question by separate Memos dated 28.09.2003, 29.09.2003 and 15.06.2004 issued by RAJUK. Since purchase of the said flats along with proportionate undivided and undemarcated share in the property in question as bonafide purchasers for value without notice of any adverse inters of encumbrance, the petitioners have been peacefully occupying their respective flats populating their names as owners with the revenue authorities and on payment of all applicable rents and levies. The petitioners were shocked to come across the impugned auction sale notice dated 

 4. Thereafter, the petitioners on inquiry/inquires learnt that respondent No. 3, Agrani Bank (the bank) instituted Artha Rin Suit No. 9 of 1991 on 16.03.1991 in the Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) and Artha Rin Adalat Joypurhat (respondent No. 2) impleading Northern Distilleries Limited and 13 others as defendants for recovery of TK. 9,94,76,565.15. The petitioners were not parties to the suit, so they had no knowledge about the suit. A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed was impleaded as defendant No. 9 in the suit. From the plaint of the said suit, it is apparent that it was filed for recovery of loans outstanding against certain credit facilities extended to Northern Distilleries Limited since 1985. In paragraph 5 of the plaint, it was averred that defendant No. 9 mortgaged the property in question in favour of the bank to secure the said credit facilities. No particulars of such mortgage were averred in the plaint However, it was stated that defendant No. 9 had deposited a certified copy of the title deed of the property in question with the Bank but despite several requests, never submitted the original of the title deed. 

 9. The writ petitioners filed supplementary affidavit annexing the Photostat copy of the mutation of the property in question in the name of Hosna Maksuda Hena Ahmed by DIT. 

 10. The Rule was opposed by the bank by filing an affidavit-in-opposition contending, inter-alia, that it as mortgagee of the property in question was entitled to satisfy its decree by sale of the mortgaged property and as such, there was no illegality in publishing the notice for auction sale of the mortgaged property. The petitioners' claim over the property in question is subject to the mortgage in favour of the Bank. In the writ petition it was stated that the property in question was sold to the Green Housing on 28.02.1995 by registered deed No. 2933, whereas the same was mortgaged to the Bank in 1986 i.e. long before the alleged transfer to the Green Housing. So, the purchase was subject to the mortgage in favour of the Bank. Once the property was mortgaged then who ever purchases the same the right of the mortgagee shall remain attached to the property. The copies of the deed of equitable mortgage, power of attorney executed by Mahbub Husain Khan to the Bank, Foreign Exchange Branch and a forwarding letter sent by Mahbub Hussain Khan (executive Director of Northern Distilleries Limited) have already been annexed to the application for vacating the order of stay. The petitioners neither being judgment debtors in the decree passed in the suit nor parties to the execution case had any locus standi to challenge various orders passed in Artha Jari Case No. 603 of 2005 and their only remedy to claim the property as third party claimant was by filing an application under section 32 of the Ain 2003 and in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure before the executing Adalat. The petitioners without availing the said remedies filed the writ petition. The alleged right, title to and interest of the petitioners in the property in question cannot he adjudicated in writ jurisdiction. It has already been decided in Writ Petition No. 4716 of 2004 that the provision of section 37 of the Ain, 2003 is not mandatory but directory. The petitioners filed the writ petition only to delay the recovery of outstanding dues of the Bank. The writ petition being not maintainable the Rule was liable to be discharged. 

 14. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order of by the High Court Division, the writ petitioner-appellants filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 949 of 2008 before this Division and leave was granted on 15.10.2009 to consider the submissions made on behalf of the petitioners, (1) the petitioners, who are the bonafide purchasers for value without notice, had come forward for enforcement of fundamental rights guaranteed under articles 31 and 42 of the Constitution and in that view of the matter the High Court Division ought to have suspended the hearing of the writ petition till the withdrawal of the Emergency, (ii) the High Court Division wrongly discharged the Rule as not being maintainable for non-exhaustion of efficacious remedy inasmuch as the petitioners having sought to enforce fundamental rights involved in the case under article 102(1) of the Constitution, exhaustion of efficacious remedy was not necessary, (iii) the writ petition having been involved pure question of law and demonstrating patent error of law, could not he dismissed on the ground of non-maintainability, (iv) the property in question could not be auction sold as it was not mortgaged by production of original title deed and furthermore it could not be mortgaged by the borrower as neither the borrower nor his principal was the owner of the same and this fact could not be properly appreciated by the High Court Division, (v) the High Court Division failed to notice that it would have disastrous consequences if equitable mortgage can he created by deposit of certified copy of the title document, (vi) admittedly the property described in `Kha' schedule to the plaint was mortgaged to the respondent No. 3 Bank by submitting certified copy of the deed of the said property without the original deed and as per Section 58(f) of the Transfer of Property Act the said property was not at all mortgaged property and the same being free from any sorts of encumbrances the respondent No. 3 had no right to claim the said property as mortgaged property but the High Court Division; without considering those aspect of dial case committed error of law in holding that the petitioners have enough scope to file an application under section 32 of the Ain, 2003 and without considering that alternative remedy always does not bar to file writ petition under article 102 of the Constitution, (vii) `Kha.' scheduled property to the plaint of Artha Rin Suit having not been included in the power of attorney, the attorney had no authority to mortgage the same to the respondent No. 3 and in the facts and circumstances of the case of the petitioner the High Court Division ought to have declared that inclusion of the said property in the plaint was without law fid authority in spite of having alternative remedy under Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003, but the High Court Division without considering so fell into an error in discharging the Rule and (viii) the High Court Division was wrong in discharging the Rule when there was no mortgage to be enforced as could be seen from paragraph 5 of the plaint which showed that the borrowers provided alternative property when they could not produce original deed of the Gulshan property. 

 16. Dr. M. Zahir, learned Counsel, appearing   on behalf of the respondent Bank, on the other hand, has repeatedly contended that the high Court Division did not commit any error of law in discharging the Rule inasmuch as the writ petitioner-appellants had other equally efficacious remedy under section 32 of the Ain, 2003. Dr. Zahir has further contended that this Division in a number of cases has held that the Artha Rin Adalat Ain being a eparchial statute and there being specific provision in the Ain for filing appeal against the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat the appellant could not challenge the same by filing writ petition, the High Court Division rightly discharged the Rule on the ground of maintainability of the writ petition. Dr. Zahir has further contended that the property in question having been mortgaged with the Bank in the year 1986, the Green Housing purchased the same with the said encumbrance and therefore, the writ-petitioner-appellants who claimed to have purchased their respective flats from the said Housing also purchased those with the said encumbrance, therefore, they could not challenge the auction sale notice of the property in question issued by the Artha Rin Adalat in execution of the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. Dr. Zahir has lastly contended that from the framing of the writ petition, it is clear that the same was not filed for enforcement of the fundamental rights of the appellants as guaranteed in Part III of the Constitution, but it was filed under article 102 thereof, so, the appellants cannot fall back upon the provisions of fundamental rights as guaranteed in the Constitution to make the writ petition maintainable, the High Court Division did not commit any error of law in discharging the Rule and as such, the appeal is liable to be dismissed. 

 17. In reply to the contentions of Dr. Zahir, Mr. Mahmudul Islam has submitted that the High Court Division in exercising power under article 102(1) of the Constitution does not give decree; but declares an action to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. And seeking relief in a particular way cannot deprive a person, here the writ-petitioners to get declaration and enforcement of their fundamental right if the context of the case demands so. He has further submitted that if the judgment and decree passed in the Artha Rin suit, the impugned auction sale notice and proceedings of the Artha Jari Case are declared to have been passed and taken without lawful authority and are of no legal effect, those will be void. Therefore, the appellants were not required to go to the executing Court taking the shelter of section 32 of the Ain, 2003 and in the context the welt petition was quite maintainable in law and as such, the High Court Division fell into an error in not declaring so. Mr. Islam has lastly submitted that the executing Court cannot go beyond the decree and the appellants not being parties to the suit and the mortgage on which the decree was passed itself being a nullity, they were not required to go to the executing Court to avail of the forum provided in section 32 of the Ain, 2003, the High Court Division was wrong in discharging the Rule on the ground of non-exhaustion of alternative remedy. 

 21. In spite of coming to the above findings, the High Court Division considered the claim of the writ-petitioners to the property in question on merit and held that whether A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed who became the owner of the property in question by purchase from the original allottee transferred the same by way of oral gift to his wife Hosne Maksuda Hena Ahmed in 1972 and whether in 1986 A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed had any interest therein are complicated questions and to decide those, the question of title to the properly has to be determined and that would require evidence, both oral and documentary. The High Court Division further observed that oral and documentary evidence will also be necessary Co-determine whether there was any valid gift in favour of the wife under the Mohamedan law; oral gift is valid provided offer, acceptance and delivery of possession in favour of the done by the donor is proved; here, the donor and the done being husband and wife, physical delivery of possession may not be necessity), and the alleged oral gift having been made in London physical possession of the property situated in Dhaka was not possible at time of making the oral gift. However, there must be some other acts to show that the gift was acted upon but there is nothing to show that the house was mutated in the name of the wife in the Government records (revenue authority) for the purpose of paying Municipal Taxes; unless there is such evidence, it cannot be said that the gift in favor of the wife by A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed was acted upon and if it was not acted upon, the gift will not be valid and all subsequent gift or transfers will become questionable. The learned Judges further observed that though mutation was done in the records of RAJUK, but there was nothing to show that the 'house' was mutated in the name of the wife in the records of the revenue authority or in the Municipal records. The learned Judges went on to observe 

 "It is interesting to note that admittedly, Mr. A.B. Shafiquddin was a senior office of the bank and loan was obtained from the bank in lieu or mortgage of the properties of Shafiquddin. Naturally, doubt may arise whether all the transactions were real transactions. If Shafiquddin was given the power of attorney by his sons to transfer the property then there (sic) no necessity of oral gift first in favour of the wife and then by the wife to their sons and then again appointment of the father as attorney by the sons it cannot he said that Mr. A.B. Shafiquddin had no interest in the property in 1986. In view of this position, the judgment and decree and the execution case wherein the property mortgaged by A.B. Shafiquddin has been put to auction sale by the impugned auction notice, cannot be declared to be without jurisdiction and without any lawful authority". 

 22. The High Court Division further found that according to the plaint, the original title deed of the mortgaged property was not deposited with the Bank as required in case of equitable mortgage and the Bank should have taken in its custody the original title deed before granting any loan to the defendants to the suit. The High Court Division noticed that the irrevocable power of attorney executed by A.B. Shafiquddin Ahmed appointing Mahbub Husain Khan as his constituted attorney to sell, mortgage etc do not contain "any schedule of properties". The properties owned by A.B. Shafiquddin Ahmed have not at all been described in the document. The High Court Division observed "We fail to understand why the Bank accepted the mortgage of the property from Mahbub Hussain Khan without bothering to verify this power of attorney executed by A.B. Shafiquddin Ahmed which is not also a registered one." Finally, the High Court Division opined that "even if the petitioners may have a good arguable case" but the same must be decided on merits by the executing Adalat or by a civil Court in accordance with law by taking proper evidence and if so advised, the petitioners may ventilate their grievance in the appropriate forum. 

 23. In view of the findings of the High Court Division, the leave granting order and the submissions of the learned Counsel for the appellants and the learned Counsel for the respondent-bank, we would like to decide first as to whether the writ petition was maintainable. As already stated hereinbefore, the High Court Division found the writ petition not maintainable   for two reasons (i) the judgment and decree passed by an Artha Rin Adalat cannot be challenged in writ jurisdiction and (ii) the petitioners had an alternative remedy under section 32 of the Ain, 2003. For the first reason, the High Court Division relied upon 3(three) decisions or this Division as noted above. On the other hand, Mr. Islam in support of his submission that the right to property is a fundamental right as enshrined in article 42 of the Constitution; admittedly mortgage of the property in question created in favour of the Bank not being a mortgage at all in the eye of law and that too tainted with fraud, the decree passed in the Artha Rin suit to realise the decretal amount by selling the said mortgaged property is a nullity and the appellants being its owners rightly challenged the same by invoking the writ jurisdiction of the High Court Division and that the availability of the alternative remedy under section 32 of the Ain, 2003 could in no way he a ground to deny the constitutional relief to the appellants, has referred to the cases of Sazedur Rahman (Md.) petitioner-vs-Secretary, Ministry of Establishment and others, 3BLC (AD) 180, H.M. Erashad-vs-Bangladesh and others 7 BLC (AD) 67 and the Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Ministry of Works and another-vs-Syed Sultana and others reported in 51 DLR(AD) 24. 

 "Although the property in question is situated in Road No. 138, the 'Kha' list mentions the property to be situated at Road No. 137. Such a notice, the High Court Division held, cannot he considered to be a notice in the eye of law and the treatment of the property in question as an abandoned property and enlisting it in the `Kha' list is without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. The writ-petitioners need not have invoked the jurisdiction of the Court of Settlement because the very inclusion of the property in question in the `Kha' list is ex facie void for want of jurisdiction and is violative of Article 42 of the Constitution." 

 26. But the question in this case is whether the judgment and decree passed by the Artha lain Adalat in Money Suit No. 9 of 1991 could be challenged by the appellants by invoking writ jurisdiction of the High Court Division. This question was precisely raised before this Division and has been answered in the negative in number of cases out of which the High Court Division rightly relied on the three cases as discussed above. We do not see any reason to take a view different from those 3(three) cases and we reiterate the statement of law that the judgment and decree passed by an Artha Kin Adalat cannot he called in question in writ jurisdiction of the high Court Division and accordingly, we find substance in the submissions of Dr. M. Zahir and confirm the decision of the High Court Division in that respect. In view of the above, we are not required to dwell upon the findings of the high Court Division on the legality of order No. 9 dated 16.07.2006 passed in the Artha Jari case allowing the prayer for amendment of the Artha Jari case and the Artha Jari proceedings itself. 

 28. From the admitted facts as stated in paragraph 5 of the plaint of the Artha Rin ,suit, it appears that the property in question was mortgaged with the respondent-basic by one Mahbub Husain Khan as the Managing Director (Executive Director) of the loance company Northern Distilleries Limited on the basis of power of attorney given by A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed by depositing the certified copy of the title deed. And when the Bank gave repeated tagid to said Mahbub Husain Khan to deposit the original title deed, he deposited the original title deeds of two other properties of the two Directors of the -company. We consider it beneficial to quote the relevant portion of the said paragraph of the plaint: 

 "Mortgage by deposit of title-deeds—(f) Where a person in the town of Dacca, Narayangonj and Chittagong and in any other town which the Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify in this behalf, delivers to a creditor or his agent documents of title to immovable property, with intent to create a security thereon, the transaction is called a mortgage by deposit of title-deeds." 

 30. A reading of section 58(f) of the Act shows that in order to create mortgage in respect of a property delivery of the documents of title of such property to the creditor, here the Bank is a must. And the documents of title definitely mean the original one and not the certified copy. The Bank knew much about the said requirement of delivery of original title document when in the plaint it said that it gave repeated tagid to Mahbub Husain Khan to file the original title document of the property in question but he did not, even then it created the mortgage accepting the certified copy of the title deed of the property in question. And yet another shocking aspect of the case is that the power of attorney allegedly given by A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed to Mr. Mahabub Husain Khan to mortgage the property in question did not contain any schedule of property. There was also no mention of any property whatsoever   in the body of the power of attorney. We fail to understand in the absence of original documents of title of the property   in question and non-mentioning of any property of A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed in the power of attorney how the Bank could accept the mortgage and gave loan to the defendant company. Thus, we find substance in the submission of Mr. Mahmudul Islam that there was no mortgage at all of the property in question in the eye of law. The High Court Division after considering paragraph 5 of the plaint rightly observed that "Therefore, it appears that according to the plaint the original title deed of the mortgaged property was not deposited with the Bank as required in case of equitable mortgage which is also supported by the decision reported in AIR 1935 Lahore 721". So, the so-called mortgage created by Mahbub Husain Khan, in 1986 on the basis of power of attorney given by A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed did not encumber the property in question in any way. We have gone through the judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat. The Artha Rin Adalat neither framed any issue as to whether the mortgage created by Mahbub Husain Khan without depositing the document of title was a valid mortgage of the property in question or gave any finding in that respect. The judgment further shows that the Artha Rin Adalat did not consider the admitted broad fact that the power of attorney given by A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed in favour of Mahbub Husain Khan did not contain any schedule of the property in question in respect of which he was appointed the attorney. The Artha Rin Adalat also failed to consider that the power of attorney was not even registered and it passed the decree in a very casual manner. Therefore, the case of the Bank that since the property in question was mortgaged with it, in 1986, the purchase of Green Housing from Abrar Atric Ahmed and Esrar Abin Ahmed through their attorney was subject to mortgage is not factually and legally acceptable and consequently the same cannot be the subject of sale in execution of the decree passed in the Money Suit No. 9 of 1991. 

 31. Admittedly A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed became the owner of the property in question by way of purchase from the original lessee Qazi Mesbahuzzman by registered deed being No. 7392 dated 24.09.1971. His name was mutated by DIT by Memo No. DIT/EO/1489 dated 26.11.1971. Appellants' case is that A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed orally gifted the property in question to his wife, Hosna Maksuda Hena Ahmed on 01.01.1972. The name of Hosna Maksuda Hena Ahmed was mutated by DIT which fact was intimated to her by Memo No. DIT/EO/729 dated 08.07.1972. Subsequently, Hosna Maksuda Hena Ahmed orally gifted the property to her two sons namely, Abrar Atric Ahmed and Esrar Abin Ahmed and the property was also mutated in the names of the latter by Rajuk vide Memo No.  RAJUK/ ESTATE/141 dated 16.01.1992. Abrar Atric Ahmed and Esrar Abin Ahmed appointed their father, A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed as their duly constituted attorney by a registered power of attorney being No. 22 dated 03.01.1994 giving him authority to manage and transfer the property in question; the power of attorney was accepted/approved by RAJUK by its Memo No.  RAJUK/ ESTATE /31781 dated 01.08.1994. Abrar Atric Ahmed and Esrar Abin Ahmed, through their attorney, A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed sold the property to Green Housing by registered deed No. 2923 dated 28.02.1995 upon obtaining permission from RAJUK by Memo No.  RAJUK/ ESTATE/542 dated; 16.02.1995. The property was then mutated in the name of the Green Housing in Mutation Case No. 12952 of 1996. Thereupon, the Green Housing constructed a 6 storied building on the property in question with 20 apartments as per approved plan of RAJUK. Out of the said 20 apartments, the Green Housing sold 12 apartments to the appellants along with proportionate undivided and undemarcated shares in the property by various deeds dated 05.06.2003 and 08.10.2004. The transfers took place upon payment of transfer fees to RAJUK and upon obtaining permission from it vide Memos dated 05.05.2003 and 01.01.2003. The names of the appellants have been mutated as owners of the apartments and co-owners of the property in question by separate Memos dated 28.09.2003, 29.09.2003 and 15.06.2004. The true copies of the appellants' deeds of purchase of the apartments from Green Housing and the Memos issued by RAJUK, mutating their names, were annexed to the writ petition as annexure -'C' C-11' and C-12' to C-22' respectively. Thus, the claim of title of the appellants to the property in question proportionate to their undivided and under interacted share starts from the oral gift made by A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed to his wife Hosna Maksuda Hena Ahmed on 01.01.1972. And if it is found that A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed gifted the property in question to his wife Hosna Maksoda Hena Ahmed on 01.01.1972 and if the same was acted upon then on and from 01.01.1972 the right, title and interest therein absolutely vested upon her and conversely on and from the said date A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed ceased to have any right, title and interest whatsoever therein. In this regard, it may be stated that on or before is July 2005, there was no necessity of registration of declaration of heba by a Mohamedan under the Muslim Personal Law (Shariat). Amendment to the above effect was brought in section 17 of the Registration Act by inserting clause (aa) therein making registration of such declaration compulsory by Act No. XXV of 2004 giving effect from 1st July 2005. 

 32. The ingredients of a valid oral gill as per Mohamedan Law is proposal by the donor to the done, acceptance of the proposal by the done followed by delivery of possession of the gifted property. In the case in hand the donor ABM Shafiquddin Ahmed is the husband of the donee Hosna Maksuda Hena Ahmed. The specific case of the appellants is that the donee accepted the gift and the donor also delivered the possession of the properly in question to the donee and thus the gift was complete. In the writ petition, it was specifically stated that after the gift, the name of Hosna Maksuda Hena Ahmed was mutated by DIT as lessee in place of ABM Shafiquddin Ahmed which fact was communicated to her vide Memo. DIT/EO/729 dated 05.07.1972. Although with the writ petition the Memo of DIT showing mutation of the name of Hosna Maksuda Hena Ahmed was not annexed, by filing a supplementary affidavit, the writ-petitioner-appellants annexed the said letter issued by DIT as annexure-'H1'. The said letter issued by DIT clearly shows that the oral gift was accepted by it and accordingly, mutated the name of Hosna Maksuda Hena Ahmed as lessee in place of A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed. In annexure-'XI' it has been clearly stated that "and henceforth you would be recognized lessee of the same". The respondent bank did not dispute this document. The very mutation of the name of Hosna 'Maksuda Hena Ahmed by the DIT, lessor, as lessee of the property in question, Prima-facie, shows that she accepted the gift made by her husband, A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed and the same was acted upon. It is true that at the time of making the gift, both the donor and donee were in London and therefore, it was not possible to take physical delivery of possession   of the property in question. The donor and the donee being husband and wife, it was sufficient to show some overt-act on the part of the donor to indicate the delivery of possession to the donee and when the name of the donee was mutated with DIT as a lessee in place of the donor, A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed it constituted sufficient indication of the overt-act of the donor. In this regard, it may further be stated that the respondent has failed to show any subsequent conduct by the donor to disown the oral gift made by him on 01.01.1972 in favour of his wife, the donee. And with the acting upon of the gift made by ABM Shafiquddin Ahmed, be divested himself of all his right, title and interest in the property in question, so he could not have any right to give power of attorney to Mahbub Husain Khan to mortgage the same in 1986. The learned Judges of the high Court Division were absolutely in error in terming the gift made by ABM Shafiquddin Ahmed as "alleged" and also in observing that "So, the pertinent question is whether A.B.M. Shafiquddin had any interest in the property in the year, 1986 when he appointed Mr. Mahbub Husain Khan as attorney. To decide this question, the question of title to the property is to be determined which is a very complicated question and requires evidence, both oral and documentary. Oral and documentary evidence will be necessary to determine whether there was any valid gift in favour of the wife". The learned judges also failed to consider that after the property in question was transferred by A.B.M. Shafiquddin to his wife Hosna Maksuda Hena Ahmed by way of oral gift which was already acted upon, she became the absolute owner thereof and had every right to deal with it in any lawful manner she liked and thus there was nothing wrong to transfer the same by way of oral gift to her two sons and when the sons became the owners of the property there was nothing wrong in appointing their father as their attorney to manage and transfer the same and the Green Housing rightly purchased the same with prior permission of RAJUK. It is also noteworthy that after purchasing the property in question Green Housing mutated its name with RAJUK and constructed at storied building with 20 flats/apartments therein after obtaining plan from RAJUK and the appellants purchased the 12 flats/apartments with proportionate undivided and undemarcated shares in the property in question by various deeds with permission from RAJUK on payment of transfer fees to it and their names were also mutated as owners of the respective apartments and co-owners of the property in question. What more is necessary to show that there had been subsequent devolution of interest in the property in question upto the appellants since Hosna Maksuda Hena Ahmed became its owner through the oral gift made by her husband A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed? 

 33. The High Court Division found fault with the title of Hosna Maksuda Hena Ahmed in the property in question on the basis of the oral gift made by A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed on the ground that her name was mutated only with RAJUK and not "in the Government records (revenue authority) for the purpose of paying rents and in the Municipal records for the purpose   of paying municipal taxes" totally forgetting that it is the RAJUK which is the lessor of the same. And non recording, of her name with the two other authorities in no way would disprove her title which she had already acquired from her husband through the gift made in her favour as back as on 01.01.1972, whereas the alleged mortgage was created only in 1986 on the basis of an alleged unregistered power of attorney and that too without mentioning of any property whatsoever of the principal. 

 35. This Division refused to accept the case of the respondent of becoming the owner of the property on the basis of the deed of gift dated 26.02.1965 on the ground that she failed to produce the original deed of gift and no paper was filed showing mutation of her name with DIT and any authority including the municipality or any document from which it could be found that she got implied possession of the property or that there was acceptance of the gift. The facts of the instant case are quite differentiable from the said reported case. In the instant case as already discussed hereinbefore after the gift, the name of Hosna Maksuda Hena Ahmed was mutated with the lessor, namely, DIT now RAJUK and then the name of the successive transferees who stepped into her shoes were mutated with RAJUK which facts, prima-facie, suggest that the gift made by A.B.M. Shafiquddin Ahmed in favour of Hosna Maksuda Hena Ahmed was acted upon. 

 (a) The oral gift of the property in question made by ABM Shafiquddin Ahmed on 01.01.1972 in favour of his wife Hosna Maksuda Hena Ahmed was acted upon and since that date, she became its absolute owner. A.B.M. Siddique had  no title in the; property in question in 1986 to execute any power of attorney in favour of Mahbub Husain Khan to mortgage the same with the defendant-bank. 

 (b) The property in question was not legally mortgaged in favour of the respondent-bank since the original title deed of the same was not admittedly deposited with it as required to create an equitable mortgage under section 58(f) of the Transfer of Property Act. 

 (c) Hosna Maksuda Hena Ahmed gifted the property in question to her two sons Abrar Atric Ahmed and Esrar Abin Ahmed and the gift made to them was acted upon through mutation of their names with RAJUK vide Memo No.  RAJUK/Estate/141 dated 16.01.1992. 

 (d)  The Green Housing Ltd., a developer company, purchased the property in question from the attorney of Abrar Atric Ahmed and Esrar Abin Ahmed vide kabala No. 2923 dated 28.02.1994 after obtaining permission from RAJUK by Memo No.  RAJUK/ Estate/542 dated 16.02.1995. Green Housing Ltd. mutated its name with the RAJUK in Mutation Case No. 12952 of 1996 and then constructed a 6(six) storied building on the property in question with 20 (twenty) apartments as per plan approved by RAJUK. 

 (h) The property of schedule-`Kha' of the decree of Money Suit No. 9 of 2991 of the Court of Subordinate Judge  and Artha Rin Adalat, Joypurhat so far as it relates to the appellants' undivided and un-demarcated share cannot be sold in auction in execution of the decree passed in the said suit. 

 36. Taking into account the admitted factual and legal aspect of the case as noted down hereinbefore, we are of the view that the, appellants have got prima-facie, valid right, title and interest in the properly in question proportionate to their undivided and under marketed share therein and their rights need be protected; it shall cause more miseries and harassment if they are pushed back to the executing Court to avail of the forum provided in section 32 of the Ain, 2003. And in the context; we consider it a fit case where the power of doing complete justice as given to this Division under article 104 of the Constitution should be exercised. And in exercise of such power, we are inclined to interfere with the judgment and decree UP passed by the Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Joypurhat in Money, Suit No. 9 of 1991 and the auction sale notice as published in the 'Daily Amar Desh' dated 18.08.2006 pursuant to the order passed by Artha Rin Adalat No. 1, Dhaka in Artha Jari Case No. 603 of 2005 for selling the properties as mentioned? Therein co-owned by the appellants. However, we approve the observations made by the High Court Division that "the Bank must take appropriate action against those officials and others involved in the loan granting process in accordance with law."
